description: Widen house.electronics.model from varchar(60) to varchar(120), through the view that reads it.
rationale: Manufacturers write model names like 'LS27AG320NLXZD Odyssey G3 27 inch 165 Hz Gaming Monitor' and 60 characters stopped being enough. Relaxing a type modifier rewrites nothing -- that is measured, not assumed -- but PostgreSQL refuses ALTER COLUMN TYPE outright while a view reads the column, whatever the change costs. So the cost here is not the rewrite; it is house.electronics_catalogue, which has to be dropped and recreated. A hand-written drop-and-recreate silently loses the view's comment, its grants, its column grants, its options, its INSTEAD OF triggers and its owner. This is the intent that puts that rebuild under test.
